Harbor & Trade

The Harbor Authority voted 6–3 late Tuesday to approve night-time dredging of the main shipping channel, overriding objections from the dockworkers' union and setting up a possible work slowdown as early as next month.

The $18 million contract, awarded to Tidewater Marine of Galveston, allows crews to operate suction dredges between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. seven days a week through March. Authority chairperson Dalia Voss said the overnight window is the only schedule that avoids colliding with daytime ferry traffic, which has grown 14 percent since the spring.

"We ran the numbers six different ways," Voss said during the hearing. "Daytime dredging costs the port roughly $2.3 million per month in lost throughput. That is a tax on every importer and exporter in the region."

Union president Marcus Oyelaran countered that overnight noise exceeds 70 decibels at the nearest residential block and that shift premiums were never negotiated. "They are trading our members' sleep for throughput statistics," he told reporters on the courthouse steps. The union filed an unfair-practice charge with the state labor board on Monday.

Under the terms approved Tuesday, Tidewater must monitor underwater noise in real time and halt work if harbor porpoise activity is detected within 400 meters of the dredge head. The environmental condition was added after a public comment period that drew more than 1,200 submissions.

Work is scheduled to begin November 3. The authority's full resolution is available on its website; the union says it will announce a formal response after its executive board meets Thursday.
